questions.question: Q: What topics does Paper 1 of OCR J271 cover?
questions.correctAnswer: Paper 1 covers two areas: Section A — The Legal System (law making through Parliament and precedent, the court system, legal personnel including judges, solicitors and barristers, and access to justice including legal aid); Section B — Criminal Law (elements of crime including actus reus and mens rea, homicide including murder and voluntary manslaughter, non-fatal offences, property offences inclu

questions.question: Q: How should you manage your time in Paper 1?
questions.correctAnswer: Paper 1 is 90 minutes for 80 marks — roughly 1 minute per mark. For a 15-mark question, spend about 15 minutes (2-3 minutes planning, 10-12 minutes writing, 1-2 minutes checking). For shorter questions, keep answers proportionate. Leave 2-3 minutes at the end to review your answers. Never spend so long on one question that you cannot attempt others.

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between Section A and Section B question technique?
questions.correctAnswer: Section A (Legal System) questions tend to be more knowledge-based — they require accurate recall of legal structures, processes and personnel. Section B (Criminal Law) questions are more likely to include problem scenarios that require application — using the ILAC method to apply legal rules to the facts. Both sections can include evaluation questions requiring balanced analysis.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Paper 1: The Legal System Technique

questions.question: Q: How many points should you make for a 4-mark question?
questions.correctAnswer: For a 4-mark question, aim for four distinct, relevant points. Each point should be a separate piece of information — do not repeat the same point in different words. Be concise: one sentence per point is usually sufficient. Do not write an essay for a short-answer question.

questions.question: Q: What should you do if you run out of time on Paper 1?
questions.correctAnswer: If running out of time, prioritise attempting all questions — even a brief answer can gain marks, while a blank answer scores zero. For a 15-mark question, write at least a brief introduction and conclusion with one or two key points rather than leaving it blank. For short answers, give the key points concisely rather than writing in full sentences.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response How should you structure your approach to Paper 1 of OCR J271 GCSE Law? (15 marks) <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A successful approach to Paper 1 requires careful planning, time management and appropriate technique for each question type. Before the exam, revise both Section A (The Legal System) and Section B (Criminal Law) thoroughly, ensuring you know key cases, statutes and legal terminology for each topic. When you open the paper, spend 2-3 minutes reading through all questions and planning your time — with 90 minutes for 80 marks, allocate roughly 1 minute per mark. Start with the questions you feel most confident about, as this builds momentum. For short-answer questions (1-4 marks), give concise, direct responses with one point per mark — no elaboration is needed. For medium-answer questions (5-10 marks), use PEEL paragraphs: make a point, provide evidence (a case or statute), explain the connection and link back to the question. For 15-mark evaluation questions, use a structured essay: brief introduction, two to three paragraphs of balanced analysis presenting both sides with specific legal examples, and a justified conclusion. For criminal law problem questions in Section B, use the ILAC method: identify the legal issue, state the relevant law (actus reus, mens rea, defences), apply the law to the specific facts of the scenario, and reach a conclusion. Always check the command word before writing and ensure your answer matches what is asked. Finally, leave 2-3 minutes at the end to review your answers for errors or omissions. This systematic approach ensures you maximise marks
